articles.headline: Premier League VAR review: Was Rice lucky not to be sent off at Brighton?
articles.description: VAR often causes controversy, but how are decisions made? Our resident ref, Andy Davies, explains all.
articles.body:
The video assistant referee causes controversy every week, whether it be the Premier League, Champions League or FA Cup, but how are those decisions made and are they correct?

For the 2026-27 season, we are taking a look at the major incidents to explain the process in terms of both VAR protocol and the laws of the game. The most surprising, controversial and complicated decisions will be examined all season long right here.

 Andy Davies (@andydaviesref) is a former Select Group referee, with over 12 seasons on the elite list, working across the Premier League and Championship. With extensive experience at the elite level, he has operated within the VAR space in the Premier League and offers a unique insight into the processes, rationale and protocols that are delivered on a matchday. 

Was Rice lucky not to be sent off at Brighton?

Brighton & Hove Albion 3-0 Arsenal (Sept. 19)

Referee: Darren England

VAR: Tim Wood

Time: 90+7 minutes

Incident: Possible red card for Arsenal's Declan Rice

What happened: Rice picked up a late yellow card when he appeared to kick out at Brighton's Malick Yalcouyé in an off-the-ball incident.

VAR decision: The on-field decision of yellow card was checked and cleared as correct by the VAR.

In these types of situations, VAR involvement can only be triggered if they believe the on-field refereeing team have missed a violent act or an act or brutality. VAR was comfortable that the action by Rice did not meet either threshold, therefore the check was a straightforward one.

Verdict: This frustrated act by Rice was picked up in real time by the fourth official and certainly high risk, when considering many off-the-ball, non-footballing offenses are often interpreted as a red-card offense by referees and matched by the expectations of football, so Rice can consider himself fortunate. However, I am comfortable that this action in isolation was a frustrated and petulant attempt at a trip on Yalcouyé and not a violent or act of brutality, therefore a yellow card feels like a correct and sensible outcome.

VAR would never get involved in this situation unless there was clear evidence that the on-field outcome was incorrect, so the yellow card was correctly checked and cleared. Rice is very fortunate that the original on-field interpretation of his action was only a yellow card, otherwise he would be serving a three-game ban following the international break.

Manchester United 0-1 Manchester City (Sept. 13)

Referee: Michael Oliver

VAR: Matt Donohue

Official Sunday inactives should begin coming in approximately 90 minutes before the scheduled kickoff times: around 11:30 a.m. ET for the early games and 2:30 p.m. ET for the late-afternoon games.

Refresh often for the latest information.

Don't forget to check these out: Mike Clay's Playbook | Week 2 Buzz

Biggest concerns heading into Week 2

Players with early starts

Zay Flowers, WR, Ravens (hamstring): Flowers was on his way to a monstrous Week 1 performance when he exited because of a hamstring injury that caused him to miss the first two days of practice this week. He did return to the field Friday, giving him a chance to suit up in Week 2. However, he is officially doubtful to go. If Flowers were to suit up this week, there is added risk that he could once again exit early.

If he sits, Rashod Bateman would be the No. 1 WR option for Lamar Jackson and would bring upside for fantasy, even if the floor is low. Mark Andrews should be started as a TE1. Some streaming options this week include Jalen Coker, Caleb Douglas, Devaughn Vele, plus a sleeper for this week, DeMario Douglas.

Joe Burrow, QB, Bengals (back): Burrow is dealing with back soreness and is listed as questionable but is expected to start. The quarterback stated that it would be "ridiculous" if the injury caused him to miss Week 2. Even in a tough matchup like the Texans, Burrow is a fantasy QB1.

If you want to avoid the matchup, Jaxson Dart and Brock Purdy are realistic options that a fantasy manager could have backing up Burrow. If you're skittish, those two could be started over him. However, for most of you, the choice should be to ride with Burrow.

TreVeyon Henderson, RB, Patriots (ankle): After missing the Patriots' opener because of an ankle injury, Henderson returned to practice this week and says he is "ready to go" for Week 2. Henderson will share work in the backfield with Rhamondre Stevenson. However, he is the more explosive option and therefore brings more fantasy upside.

Henderson can be played over Quinshon Judkins, MarShawn Lloyd, Tony Pollard, J.K. Dobbins, Rico Dowdle, Blake Corum, Kenny Gainwell and Jonathon Brooks.

Jalen Coker, WR, Panthers (ankle): After a huge Week 1 performance, Coker was limited in practice to start the week because of an ankle injury. articles.headline: Prosecutors identify 18 alleged rigged pitches for Clase trial
articles.description: Prosecutors identified 18 pitches, including one from a 2024 playoff game, that will be the focus of their case against Guardians closer Emmanuel Clase that is set for trial in November, according to court documents.
articles.body:
Federal prosecutors have identified 18 pitches, including one from a 2024 playoff game, that will be the focus of their gambling case against Cleveland Guardians closer Emmanuel Clase, which is set for trial in November, according to court documents filed Friday.

In the documents, prosecutors from the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of New York included a list of the individual pitches that Clase threw in 17 games spanning from May 19, 2023, to May 28, 2025. Clase is accused of sharing advance information about the pitches with bettors, who allegedly placed wagers on the result and velocity of the pitches.

Clase's first pitch to Matt Vierling of the Detroit Tigers in the ninth inning of an Oct. 5, 2024, American League Division Series game was on the list. The pitch, a 93 mph slider, was out of the strike zone. The Guardians won the game 7-0.

Prosecutors allege that Guardians starter Luis Ortiz also participated in the scheme by giving bettors advance information about two of his pitches but did not identify them in the filings.

Clase, Ortiz and two other defendants face wire fraud, money laundering and conspiracy charges. They have pleaded not guilty. Jury selection for the trial is set to begin in November.

In February, the government provided Clase and Ortiz's attorneys with a preliminary list of pitches it was investigating. Ortiz's attorney wrote in a filing at the time that prosecutors had accused Clase of throwing suspect pitches in at least 48 games.

Prosecutors are now focused on 18 pitches from 17 games ahead of the trial, according to the documents.

"The government will only seek to prove that for one or more of approximately 18 of Clase's pitches, and for two of Ortiz's pitches, the defendants provided advance inside information about their pitches to others, who bet on them," U.S. attorney Joseph Nocella wrote.

Clase and Ortiz have been on leave since the summer of 2025. Sportsbooks flagged unusual betting interest on specific pitches from Ortiz in two games in June 2025.

articles.headline: Rams' Puka Nacua again misses practice, questionable for MNF
articles.description: Rams receiver Puka Nacua will not practice for the second day in a row and will be listed as questionable for Monday night's game against the Giants.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua will not practice for the second day in a row due to "a little bit of soreness" in his groin and will be listed as questionable for Monday night's game against the New York Giants, coach Sean McVay said.

"[We are] being smart with him as a skill player," McVay said Saturday. "Whether or not he plays is to be determined. And so we'll see how he's feeling, but he won't practice [Saturday]."

McVay said Nacua's injury is separate from the psoas injury that caused him to miss time during training camp.

Nacua practiced Thursday, McVay said, but he "didn't feel totally like himself [with] his ability to be able to kind of open up and really hit full speed." He was listed on the injury report Friday with a hip injury.

McVay also said wide receiver Jordan Whittington, who was added to the injury report Friday, will be listed as doubtful for the game with a quad injury.

The Rams are expecting Aaron Donald to play Monday night in what would be his first game since coming out of retirement after two seasons. When asked Friday if he would play, Donald said "that's the plan."

"If he said it, he's going," McVay said Saturday. "Whatever Aaron says, I support him."

articles.headline: Liam Rosenior taunts Strasbourg fans, causes melee: 'They disrespected my family'
articles.description: Liam Rosenior has caused controversy after he went over to celebrate Paris FC's 2-1 home win over his former club Strasbourg in front of the travelling fans, leading to a physical confrontation between players and staff from both teams.
articles.body:
Liam Rosenior has caused controversy after he went over to celebrate Paris FC's 2-1 home win over his former club Strasbourg in front of the travelling fans, leading to a physical confrontation between players and staff from both teams.

Rosenior, who spent 18 months as Strasbourg head coach prior to joining Chelsea and is now the Paris FC boss, could be seen pointing his finger, slapping his chest and raising his arms to the Strasbourg fans after the final whistle on Saturday.

Within seconds, around 30 people sprinted over and a mass shoving match ensued.

In his post-match news conference, Rosenior accused some members of the Strasbourg fans of insulting his family.

"[There was a small part of the Strasbourg] support who disrespect my family," he said. "I understand the context of what they were saying. My bench were visibly upset.

"I want to make this very clear: a small section. Strasbourg is a fantastic football club, with great people who work for the club, and great people who support the club.

"For me to celebrate in that way was a message. A message to a group of people who never wanted me to be successful at that club. But I'm not going to say anymore than that."

Rosenior also addressed the incident in a post-match interview with Ligue 1+.

"The people in the club [Strasbourg] who know me know I've always been respectful, I've always wanted the best for that football club," he said. "I still do want the best for that football club.

"But when I heard the chants -- I understand French, I understand the context, the language -- that's a step too far.

"It's a wonderful football club, it's a great city, it's a club with great tradition, I've always protected those traditions.

"So for me to celebrate in the way that I did, was for many reasons. Many reasons."

- Xabi Alonso says Chelsea were 'out of control' in Brentford loss

- USMNT's Balogun makes season debut for Monaco after failed transfer

- PSG ultras take legal action over Marseille travel ban

Goals from Ilan Kebbal and Pablo Pagis gave Paris FC the win despite a late own goal by Moustapha Mbow.

The Paris side have made an excellent start in Rosenior's first season at the club, remaining unbeaten with three wins from five games.

They sit second in Ligue 1, two points behind Monaco and six points ahead of Paris Saint-Germain, who have played a game fewer.

articles.headline: European soccer recap: Brighton humble Arsenal, Villa keep Spurs winless
articles.description: Another weekend of European soccer action continues with Brighton & Hove Albion hosting Premier League leaders and defending champions Arsenal.
articles.body:
It's another weekend of European soccer and the final one before the international break!

In the Premier League, Saturday's action began with Aston Villa beating Tottenham Hotspur 3-2 in London. Both teams were chasing their first league victory of the season and, while Spurs are still winless and in the bottom three, they did score their first goals on the campaign.

Next up, Brighton & Hove Albion welcomed league leaders Arsenal to England's south coast, and promptly dispatched the defending champions 3-0. Finally, Nottingham Forest host a Coventry City side still searching for their first win and goal of the season.

Elsewhere, AS Roma settled for a 2-2 with Inter Milan in a huge clash between Serie A's current top two. In the Bundesliga, Stuttgart fell 1-0 to Borussia Dortmund, while in LaLiga, Sevilla host league leaders Barcelona.

Enjoy all the updates from Saturday's matches.

articles.headline: Coventry claim first Premier League win of season at Nottingham Forest
articles.description: Jay DaSilva fired Coventry to their first Premier League win in 25 years as they beat Nottingham Forest 1-0 in another game mired by VAR controversy.
articles.body:
Jay DaSilva fired Coventry to their first Premier League win in 25 years as they beat Nottingham Forest 1-0 in another game mired by VAR controversy.

Frank Lampard's side have endured a tough return to the top flight, with four defeats and no goals, but they put that right at the fifth attempt at the City Ground on a memorable night.

DaSilva's second-half strike ended their drought and proved enough for a first three points in the top division since the Sky Blues beat Sunderland back in April 2001.

Forest thought they had found a late leveller when Igor Jesus slotted home, but referee Jared Gillett was sent to the monitor by VAR and ruled there was a foul on Caleb Yirenkyi, despite his original on-field decision being a goal.

It left Forest with a burning sense of injustice but, in truth, they did not do enough to take anything from the game.

They are having trouble at the City Ground, having won there just once in the league in front of their own fans since December last year.

The VAR decision means Oliver Glasner's men have yet to score in their first three home games, and it is undermining promising away form where they have taken four points from trips to Liverpool and Aston Villa.

After winning at Villa Park last week, Forest were full of confidence and were straight on the attack, with James McAtee shooting straight at Carl Rushworth from distance after just 50 seconds.

McAtee had another goalbound shot blocked as the Forest attacks kept on coming, with Dan Ndoye unable to finish a nice move by curling just over from 18 yards in the 18th minute.

Liam Delap also had an effort from distance that hit the side-netting as Forest probed without creating anything.

Glasner's men were on the front foot again early in the second half as McAtee had a third effort of the day.

Ndoye and Delap combined down the left, with the striker teeing up the former Manchester City midfielder, but his shot was superbly blocked by Ethan Pinnock.

That proved pivotal as Coventry got a foothold in the game, with Loum Tchaouna shooting straight at Matz Sels.

But Coventry's patient fans finally got their moment 10 minutes into the second half as DaSilva broke their duck.

He raced on to Carl Rushworth's long kick, beat Daniel Munoz, and then fired home in front of the jubilant supporters.

Forest had little in the way of an immediate response as frustrations began to grow.

They began to up the ante in the final 15 minutes and almost levelled when substitute Jesus was denied

by Bobby Thomas' acrobatic clearance off the line.

They had the ball in the back of the net in the 86th minute as Jesus took advantage of a slip by Yirenkyi to roll home.

But for the second home match in a row VAR got involved, with Gillett changing his decision after viewing the monitor and ruling Jesus had clipped the Coventry defender's ankle.

articles.headline: Arsenal 'in trouble from first throw-in' at Brighton - Mikel Arteta
articles.description: Mikel Arteta said he knew Arsenal would be "in trouble" from "the first throw-in" in a 3-0 defeat at Brighton.
articles.headlineJa: ブライトン戦のアーセナルは「最初のスローインから苦しんでいた」― ミケル・アルテタ
articles.descriptionJa: ミケル・アルテタ監督は、ブライトンに0-3で敗れた試合で「最初のスローインから」アーセナルが苦戦すると分かっていたと明かした。
articles.body:
BRIGHTON, England -- Mikel Arteta said he knew Arsenal would be "in trouble" from "the first throw-in" in a 3-0 defeat at Brighton that ended the champions' unbeaten start to the defence of their Premier League title.

Goals from Pascal Gross, Charalampos Kostoulas and Chema Andrés sealed a convincing and deserved victory for the home side, who climbed to third in the table on the back of the win.

It was the first time Arsenal had lost by three goals in the Premier League since Brighton defeated the Gunners 3-0 at the Emirates in May 2023 and Fabian Hurzeler's side were dominant throughout the game.

But after seeing his side drop points for the first time this season, Arteta said Arsenal had no excuses at the Amex.

"I'm extremely disappointed, but first of all, we have to congratulate Brighton for the victory because they deserved it," Arteta said. "They were the better team.

"From our side, there are certain basics that you need to accomplish in the Premier League, but we were very far from [winning] the first duel, the second duel and that put us in a difficult place.

"We made lots of errors, we had no principles of play in situations and we were always on back foot.

"At end of the day, it's a big lesson for us, for all of us."

Brighton coasted to the win despite having 24 hours less recovery time following the midweek Carabao Cup programme. Hurzeler's side won 3-2 at Manchester United on Wednesday while a much-changed Arsenal side beat Ipswich 4-2 at Portman Road on Tuesday.

But despite the advantages in his team's favour, Arteta said that Brighton showed more "bite" and he knew his side would have a bad day "from the first throw-in."

"They [Brighton] knew, we knew, how tough it would be today," Arteta said. "But Brighton overcame us and had another edge that we didn't have.

"Brighton had another bite, their timing was better and when the ball was 50-50, most of the time it was for them.

- Brighton vs. Arsenal player ratings as Gunners slump to hefty defeat against Seagulls

- Transfer rumors, news: Arsenal's Madueke eyed by Premier League rivals

"From the first throw-in, it was clear that we would be in trouble. We were extremely poor technically and not respecting the game.

"Credit to Brighton. It doesn't take away from what the team has done the last few weeks.

"But now we have to make sure we learn the lesson because this can happen again."
